declared_token_position.meaning: address value occupying the token position of the ClaimRecipientUpdated event as declared

declared_recipient_position.meaning: address value occupying the recipient position of the ClaimRecipientUpdated event as declared

emitted_token_topic.meaning: address actually carried in the indexed token topic of the emitted log

emitted_recipient_topic.meaning: address actually carried in the recipient topic of the emitted log

stored_claim_token.meaning: token key of claimRecipient[user][token] written by _setClaimRecipient

stored_claim_recipient.meaning: recipient address stored as claimRecipient[user][token] by _setClaimRecipient

assumptions: Off-chain reporting, accounting and payout automation rely on the event topics to determine recipients rather than reading on-chain storage.
No concrete submitted transaction, user or token values are reported, so the scenario is a possible configuration of symbolic addresses.

unresolved.description: The report does not state whether the emitted arguments are swapped relative to a declared (user, token, recipient) order in a way that can be compared to storage beyond the topic-position mismatch; the relation between emitted topics and stored key/recipient is asserted only qualitatively.

limitations: Direct off-chain mispairing impact indexers_construct_inverse_mapping is deferred to a separate claim.
No numeric bounds, authorization conditions, or indexer-side state are formalized in this core relation.
The plan models event topic positions as observable address symbols; code-level topic hashing and indexing mechanics are outside this core semantic claim.
The mismatch is treated as a state-correspondence relation between declared/emitted event fields and stored mapping values, not as an access-control or liveness property.
